<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">and Other Postemployment Benefits,
</font></i>as amended (see below)<i><font style="font-style:italic;">.</font></i>&nbsp; SFAS No. 132 establishes standards for
employers who provide benefits to former or inactive employees after employment
but before retirement.&nbsp; Postemployment benefits include, but are not
limited to, salary continuation, supplemental employment benefits and
disability related benefits.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Earnings/ Loss per Common Share</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company
calculates earnings or loss per common share in accordance with SFAS No. 128, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Earnings Per Share</font></i>.&nbsp; Accordingly,
basic loss per common share excludes dilution for potentially dilutive
securities and is computed by dividing net loss available to common
shareholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for
the period (See Note 8). Diluted earnings per common share reflects the
potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue
common stock were exercised or converted into common stock. When a company is
in a loss position, basic and diluted loss per common share are the same.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Significant Recent Accounting
Pronouncements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2003, the FASB issued FASB
Interpretation (&#147;FIN&#148;) No.&nbsp;46, &#147;Consolidation of Variable Interest
Entities, an Interpretation of ARB No.&nbsp;51.&#148; The primary objectives of FIN
No.&nbsp;46 are to provide guidance on the identification of entities for which
control is achieved through means other than voting rights (variable interest
entities, or &#147;VIEs&#148;), and how to determine when and which business enterprise
should consolidate the VIE. This new model for consolidation applies to an
entity for which either: (a)&nbsp;the equity investors do not have a
controlling financial interest; or (b)&nbsp;the equity investment at risk is
insufficient to finance that entity&#146;s activities without receiving additional
subordinated financial support from other parties. In addition, FIN No.&nbsp;46
requires that both the primary beneficiary and all other enterprises with a
significant variable interest in a VIE make additional disclosures. As amended
in December&nbsp;2003, the effective dates of FIN No.&nbsp;46 for public
entities that are not small business issuers are as follows: (a)&nbsp;For
interests in special-purpose entities: the first period ended after
December&nbsp;15, 2003; and (b)&nbsp;For all other types of VIEs: the first
period ended after March&nbsp;15, 2004. Management has determined that the
Company does not have any VIEs, and there is no impact on its consolidated
financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2003, the FASB issued SFAS
No.&nbsp;149, &#147;Amendments of Statement 133 on Derivative Instruments and
Hedging Activities,&#148; which amends and clarifies financial accounting and
reporting for derivative instruments, including certain derivative instruments
embedded in other contracts and for hedging activities under SFAS No.&nbsp;133.
This pronouncement is effective for contracts entered into or modified after
June&nbsp;30, 2003 (with certain exceptions), and for hedging relationships
designated after June&nbsp;30, 2003. The adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;149 did not
have a material impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2003, the FASB issued SFAS
No.&nbsp;150, &#147;Accounting for Certain Financial Instruments with Characteristics
of both Liabilities and Equity.&#148; SFAS No.&nbsp;150 establishes standards for
how a company classifies and measures certain financial instruments with
characteristics of both liabilities and equity, and is effective for public
companies as follows: (i)&nbsp;in November&nbsp;2003, the FASB issued FASB
Staff Position (&#147;FSP&#148;) FAS&nbsp;150-03 (&#147;FSP 150-3&#148;), which defers indefinitely
(a)&nbsp;the measurement and classification guidance of SFAS No.&nbsp;150 for
all mandatorily redeemable non-controlling interests in (and issued by)
limited-life consolidated subsidiaries, and (b)&nbsp;SFAS No.&nbsp;150&#146;s
measurement guidance for other types of mandatorily redeemable non-controlling
interests, provided they were created before November&nbsp;5, 2003;
(ii)&nbsp;for financial instruments entered into or modified after May&nbsp;31,
2003 that are outside the scope of FSP 150-3; and (iii)&nbsp;otherwise, at the
beginning of the first interim period beginning after June&nbsp;15, 2003. The
Company adopted SFAS No.&nbsp;150 on the aforementioned effective dates. The
adoption of this pronouncement did not have a material impact on the Company&#146;s
results of operations or financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2003, the FASB issued a
revision of SFAS No.&nbsp;132, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Employers&#146;
Disclosures about Pensions and Other Postretirement Benefits</font></i>. This
pronouncement (&#147;SFAS No.&nbsp;132-R&#148;) expands employers&#146; disclosures about
pension plans and other post-retirement benefits, but does not change the
measurement or recognition of such plans required by SFAS No.&nbsp;87,
No.&nbsp;88. or No.&nbsp;106. SFAS No.&nbsp;132-R retains the existing
disclosure requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;132, and requires certain additional
disclosures about defined benefit post-retirement plans. The defined benefit
pension plan of the Company&#146;s United Kingdom subsidiary is the Company&#146;s only
defined benefit post-retirement plan. Except as described in the following
sentence, SFAS No.&nbsp;132-R is effective for foreign pension plans for fiscal
years ending after June&nbsp;15, 2004; after the effective date, restatement
for some of the new disclosures is required for earlier annual periods. Some of
the interim-period disclosures mandated by SFAS No.&nbsp;132-R (such as the
components of net periodic benefit cost, and certain key assumptions) are
effective for foreign pension plans for quarters beginning after
December&nbsp;15, 2003; other interim-period disclosures will not be required
for the Company until the first quarter of 2005. The interim-period disclosure
requirements which became effective on January&nbsp;1, 2004 and December 31,
2004 were adopted by the Company on those dates. The Company is presently
evaluating the other effects of SFAS No.&nbsp;132-R on its interim-period
financial statement disclosures.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December 2004, the FASB issued SFAS
No.&nbsp;123-R which replaces SFAS No.&nbsp;123, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>, and supersedes APB
Opinion No.&nbsp;25, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock
Issued to Employees</font></i>. As originally issued, SFAS No.&nbsp;123
established as preferable a fair-value-based method of accounting for share-based
payment transactions with employees. However, that pronouncement permitted entities
to continue applying the intrinsic-value-based model of APB Opinion&nbsp;25,
provided that the financial statements disclosed the pro forma net income or
loss based on the fair-value method.&#160; The
Company is required to apply SFAS No.&nbsp;123-R</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-12</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">as of the first interim reporting period that begins after
June&nbsp;15, 2005. Thus, the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements will
reflect an expense for (a)&nbsp;all share-based compensation arrangements
granted after June&nbsp;30, 2005 and for any such arrangements that are
modified, cancelled, or repurchased after that date, and (b)&nbsp;the portion
of previous share-based awards for which the requisite service has not been
rendered as of that date, based on the grant-date estimated fair value of those
awards.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other recent accounting pronouncements issued
by the FASB (including its Emerging Issues Task Force), the American Institute
of Certified Public Accountants and the Securities and Exchange Commission (the
&#147;SEC&#148;), did not or are not believed by management to have a material impact on
the Company&#146;s present or future consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 2.&#160;
Divestitures and Material Licensing Agreements</font></b></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Sale of Accountor Oy</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2002, the
Company sold its 19.9% interest in Accountor Oy to Pretax Ltd, an unrelated
party.&nbsp; Under the terms of the sale, the Company&#146;s gross proceeds were
$0.8 million less transaction costs and purchase commitments (net of
reimbursements) of approximately $0.1 million.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s investment
in Accountor Oy was carried at less than $0.1 million at the time of
sale.&nbsp; Accordingly, the Company&#146;s other income for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2002 includes a pretax gain of $0.7 million on the sale of
Accountor Oy.&#160; During 2003, subsequent events
occurred that caused adjustments to the purchase price, as provided in the
original agreements.&#160; The result is the
Company&#146;s other income for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003 includes a
reduction of $0.1 million of the 2002 pretax gain on the sale of Accountor
Oy.&#160; The final pretax gain on the sale of
Accountor Oy was $0.6 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Sale of ABC Technologies- France</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2002, the
Company sold its interest in ABC Technologies &#150; France (&#147;ABC Technologies&#148;) to
an unrelated party.&nbsp; Under the terms of the sale, the Company collected
proceeds of approximately $0.3 million in 2003. Based in Paris, France, ABC
Technologies was managed by Artemis&#146; French subsidiary.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s
investment in ABC Technologies was carried at approximately zero at the time of
sale.&nbsp; Accordingly, the Company&#146;s other income for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2002 includes a pretax gain of $0.3 million on the sale of
ABC Technologies.&nbsp; Based on achieving certain milestones, an additional
$0.1 million of consideration was recorded during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Sale of Assets of Software
Productivity Research</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;2003, the
Company entered into an asset purchase agreement for the sale of its Software
Productivity Research (&#147;SPR&#148;) operations.&#160;
Total consideration received for the sale of SPR, including liabilities
assumed by the buyer, was $0.4 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Licensing Agreement with Advanced
Management Solutions</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December 2004, the Company entered into a
definitive agreement (the &#147;AMS Agreement&#148;) with Advanced Management Solutions
Inc. (&#147;AMS&#148;), a company providing Enterprise Project and Resource Management
solutions, whereby (i)&nbsp;the Company obtained the worldwide exclusive right
to use, market and grant sub-licenses with respect to certain software
developed by AMS (the &#147;AMS Software), (ii)&nbsp;AMS will provide additional
development services under direction of the Company, and (iii)&nbsp;the Company
has obtained the right to purchase the AMS Software through November&nbsp;30,
2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The initial term of the software license ends
November&nbsp;30, 2007, and is renewable for one additional three-year term.
The Company has agreed on certain minimum royalty payments to secure worldwide
exclusivity. Also as part of the transaction, the Company agreed to pay AMS
$0.5&nbsp;million to secure the option to purchase the AMS Software. This
option fee is non-recoverable on the condition that the initially delivered AMS
Software meets generally accepted industry standards. Further, the Company has
agreed to fund the additional development work with $0.5&nbsp;million to be
paid in five installments. The first such installment of $0.1 million was paid
in December 2004.&#160; The purchase price for
the AMS Software is $2.5&nbsp;million and is payable in two annual
installments, should the Company elect to exercise such option.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

amortized on a straight-line basis over their expected useful lives of
forty-two months. During the fourth quarter of 2004, the Company evaluated the
carrying values of its intangible assets and recorded an impairment charge of
approximately $0.9 million on current technologies, representing the remaining
unamortized balance. Accordingly, intangible assets and related accumulated
amortization consist entirely of the customer base at December 31, 2004. &#160;During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2004,
2003 and 2002 approximately $4.1 million of intangible assets was amortized
each year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s proprietary products are not
protected by patents.&#160; However, to
protect the Company&#146;s intellectual property rights, the Company licenses its
software products and requires its customers to enter into license agreements
that impose restrictions on their ability to utilize the software or transfer
it to other users.&#160; Additionally, the
Company seeks to avoid disclosure of its trade secrets through a number of
means, including, but not limited to, requiring those persons with access to
the Company&#146;s proprietary information to execute confidentiality agreements
with the Company and restricting access to the Company&#146;s source code.&#160; In addition, the Company protects its
software, documentation, templates and other written materials under trademark,
trade secret and copyright laws.&#160; Even
with all of these efforts, there can be no assurance that such precautions will
provide meaningful protection from competition or that competitors will not
independently be able to develop similar technology.&#160; If, in the future, litigation is necessary to
enforce the Company&#146;s intellectual property rights, to protect the Company&#146;s
trade secrets, or to determine the validity and scope of the proprietary rights
of others, such litigation could result in substantial costs and diversion of
resources and could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s business,
operating results and/or financial condition.&#160;
Ultimately, the Company may be unable, for financial or other reasons,
to enforce its rights under the various intellectual property laws as described
above.&#160; In addition, the laws of certain
countries in which the Company&#146;s products are or may be licensed may not
protect the Company&#146;s&#160; intellectual
property rights to the same extent as laws of the United States.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes that its products do not
infringe upon any valid existing proprietary rights of third parties.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 6. Debt</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2003, the
Company paid off its note payable and line of credit with Wells Fargo Foothill
(&#147;Foothill&#148;) and declined the option to extend the underlying loan and security
agreement with Foothill.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Also in June
2003, the Company obtained a bridge loan of $3.5 million from Proha, accruing
interest at 4.75% per annum, which was fully repaid by the Company during the
quarter ended September 30, 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;14, 2003, the Company entered
into an agreement with Laurus Master Fund, Ltd. (&#147;Laurus&#148;) and received a
$5.0&nbsp;million revolving credit facility (the &#147;Laurus Facility&#148;) in the form
of a three-year convertible note (the &#147;Secured Convertible Note&#148;) secured by an
interest in all of the Company&#146;s property and assets located in the United
States (US) and the United Kingdom (UK), except for intellectual property
rights. Borrowings under the Laurus Facility are based on the balance of
eligible trade accounts receivable reported by the Company&#146;s operating entities
in the US and the UK. The Laurus Facility automatically renews every three
years unless cancelled by the Company or Laurus. In conjunction with the original
transaction, Laurus was paid a fee of $175,000 and received a ten-year
transferable warrant (the &#147;Laurus Warrant&#148;) to purchase 125,000&nbsp;shares of
the Company&#146;s common stock. The estimated fair value of the Laurus Warrant of
approximately $237,000 has been treated as additional interest expense and is
being amortized over the three-year life of the Laurus Facility, unless sooner
terminated. The fair value of the Laurus Warrant was estimated based on the
following assumptions: expected volatility: 272%; dividends: zero; risk free
interest rate: 2.6%; and expected life of the warrant: five&nbsp;years. The
warrant permits Laurus to purchase up to 50,000, 50,000, and 25,000 shares of
the Company&#146;s common stock at exercise prices of $3.41, $4.10, and $4.78 per share,
respectively. The Laurus Warrant exercise price and the number of shares
underlying the warrant are subject to anti-dilution adjustments for stock
splits, combinations and dividends.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June 2004, the Company used
$2.2&nbsp;million of the net proceeds of the private placement of
$9.0&nbsp;million of convertible preferred stock (the &#147;Preferred Series A
Financing&#148;) completed on June&nbsp;16, 2004 to reduce the amount outstanding
under the Laurus Facility from $3.5&nbsp;million to $1.3&nbsp;million. On
July&nbsp;30, 2004, the Company and Laurus agreed to amend the Laurus Facility
by replacing the Secured Convertible Note of up to $5.0&nbsp;million with a
Secured Convertible Minimum Borrowing Note (the &#147;Minimum Borrowing Note&#148;) in
the amount of $1.5&nbsp;million and a Secured Revolving Note of up to
$3.5&nbsp;million (collectively the &#147;Laurus Restructuring&#148;). Effective upon the
execution of the Laurus Restructuring documents on July&nbsp;30, 2004,&#160; the $1.3&nbsp;million outstanding under the
Laurus Facility was incorporated as monies provided by Laurus under the Minimum
Borrowing Note.&#160; In August 2004, Laurus
provided Artemis an additional $0.2&nbsp;million under the Minimum Borrowing
Note, thereby exhausting the funds available to Artemis under the Minimum
Borrowing Note.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Minimum Borrowing Note is due on August&nbsp;26,
2006 and is convertible into common stock of the Company at the option of the
holder at the following prices: 190,000 shares at $1.45 per share, 190,000
shares at $1.81 per share, and 342,646 shares at $2.57 per share, totaling $1.5
million or 722,646 shares of common stock of the Company.&#160; Loans exceeding $1.5 million may be available
to the Company under the Secured Revolving Note, based on the balance of the
Company&#146;s eligible trade accounts receivable. If the balance on the Minimum
Borrowing Note is zero, such portion of the balance of the Secured Revolving
Note that exceeds $1.0 million shall be deemed to be extinguished on the
Secured Revolving Note and transferred to a new serialized Minimum Borrowing
Note. Once a new serialized Minimum Borrowing Note reaches the sum of $1.5
million, the Company is required to file a registration statement with the SEC
to register the shares underlying the new serialized Minimum Borrowing Note.
Thereafter, the conversion price adjusts to 105% of the average closing market
price of the Company&#146;s common stock for the five trading days immediately
preceding each additional serialized $1.5&nbsp;million Minimum Borrowing Note.
All of the aforementioned conversion prices are subject to an anti-dilution
provision in the form of a price protection clause. Under the terms of the
related agreement, absent an event of default as defined, conversion of the
Minimum Borrowing Note into the Company&#146;s common stock may not result in
beneficial ownership by Laurus (including shares </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-15</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">issuable under the Laurus Warrant that are exercisable within sixty
days of any determination date) of more than 2.5% of the Company&#146;s outstanding
common stock. The Minimum Borrowing Note has a 30% prepayment penalty. Any

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company filed a registration statement on
Form S-1 with the SEC on November 3, 2004 (which was amended in December 2004
and January 2005) to register the common stock underlying the Minimum Borrowing
Note and the Laurus Warrant.&#160; The SEC
declared such registration statement effective on February 3, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subsequent to December 31, 2004, Laurus
converted $0.2 million of the outstanding $1.5 million Minimum Borrowing Note
in exchange for 166,700 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;1, 2004</font><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">,</font></b> the
Company&#146;s wholly-owned subsidiary in Finland, Artemis Finland Oy (&#147;Artemis
Finland&#148;), entered into a loan agreement with a financial institution in the
amount of approximately $3.1 million which has been partially repaid subsequent
to year end (See Note 12).</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest paid for the years ended December
31, 2004, 2003 and 2002 was approximately $0.3 million, $0.1 million and $0.2
million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Diluted loss per common
share for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002 does not
include the effect of stock options and warrants (see Note 15) since their
effect would be anti-dilutive.&nbsp; Options and warrants outstanding at
December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002 approximated 2.5 million, 1.2 million and
1.3 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 9. Benefit Plans</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a defined
contribution plan (&#147;the Plan&#148;) which qualifies under Section&nbsp;401(k) of the
Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. The Plan covers all U.S. employees
who may contribute up to 15% of their annual compensation with an annual
maximum of $13,000 for calendar 2004. Employer contributions vest to the
participants incrementally over a period of five years. Company contributions
to the Plan were $54,000 during the year ended December 31, 2004 and zero
during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2003 and 2002.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company also has a
defined benefit pension plan covering the employees of its United Kingdom
subsidiary. Company contributions are determined based upon a percentage, as
determined by an actuary, of an eligible employee&#146;s annual salary.&nbsp;
Company contributions to the defined benefit pension plan during the years
ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002 were $0.5 million, $0.2 million and
$0.2 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As permitted by SFAS No. 87,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Employers&#146; Accounting for Pensions, </font></i>actuarial
gains and losses are generally not amortized to pension expense in the period
in which they arise when the gain/loss is not yet included in the
market-related value of plan assets.&nbsp; GAAP allows such deferral accounting
in any period in which the beginning-of-the-year unrecognized actuarial net
gain or loss does not exceed 10% of the greater of the projected benefit
obligation or the market-related value of plan assets.&#160; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2002,
the Company&#146;s defined benefit pension plan was eligible for the deferral accounting
described in the preceding sentence.&nbsp; Thus pension expense for 2002 does
not include any amortization of the actuarial net change in the market-related
value of plan assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">The accounting</font>
for the Company&#146;s defined benefit pension plan described above requires that an
additional minimum liability (as defined) be recorded when certain conditions
are met at the balance sheet date.&#160; Since
the Company&#146;s unrecognized prior </font>service
cost was nil at December 31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, the increase in such
liability was charged directly to stockholders&#146; deficit as a component of other
comprehensive loss.&#160; Management
determined that the Company did not reflect the additional minimum liability in
the 2002 consolidated financial statements included in its December 31, 2003
Form 10-K filed with the SEC on March 30, 2004.&#160;
The accompanying consolidated statement of stockholders&#146; equity and
comprehensive loss for the year ended December 31, 2002 was restated in July
2004 to reflect an additional minimum pension liability of approximately
$1,060,000.&#160; This adjustment did not
affect the previously reported net loss for the year ended December 31, 2002.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July 2004,
the Company also revised certain disclosures in the above tables relating to
(a) the December 31, 2003 and 2002 funded status of the pension plan and (b)
the December 31, 2003 fair value of the pension plan&#146;s assets.&#160; The differences principally resulted from the
combination of a mathematical error and misapplication of certain
financial-statement disclosure requirements.&#160;
Since the related amounts were properly reported in the previously
issued financial statements, the amended disclosures described in this
paragraph did not effect the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2004, current income tax expense consists of approximately
$0.4 million of foreign expense and approximately $0.1 million of state

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The components of deferred
tax liabilities at December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002 relate primarily to
the recording of non-deductible intangible assets from the acquisition of
Legacy Artemis by Proha in August&nbsp;2000 and the contribution of businesses
to Legacy Artemis by Proha in December&nbsp;2000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income taxes paid for the
years ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002 were less than $0.5 million
for each year.&nbsp; The Company has a U.S. federal tax net operating loss
carryforward (&#147;NOL&#148;) of approximately $28 million at December&nbsp;31, 2004
that begins expiring in 2009 and U.S. state NOL&#146;s with expiration dates ranging
from five to 20 years.&#160; Foreign NOL&#146;s that
may be allowed under the tax laws in applicable foreign countries are not
significant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The utilization of some or
all of the domestic NOL&#146;s may be severely restricted now or in the future by
the change in ownership provisions of Section&nbsp;382 of the Internal Revenue
Code of 1986, as amended.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December 2004, the FASB issued FSP 109-2, &#147;Accounting and Disclosure
Guidance for the Foreign Repatriation Provision within the American Jobs
Creation Act of 2004.&#148;&#160; FSP 109-2 states
that an enterprise is allowed time beyond the financial reporting period of
enactment to evaluate the effects of the American Jobs Creation Act of 2004
(the &#147;Act&#148;) on its plan for reinvestment or repatriation of foreign earnings
for the purposes of applying SFAS No. 109.&#160;
The Company has not yet completed evaluating the impact of the
repatriation provisions of the Act.&#160;
Given the preliminary stage of the Company&#146;s evaluation, it is not
possible at this time to determine what impact (if any) the repatriation
provisions will have on the consolidated income tax accruals or the Company&#146;s
effective income tax rate.&#160; Accordingly,
as provided by FSP 109-2, the Company has not adjusted its income tax expense
or deferred tax liability to reflect the repatriation provisions of the Act.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fourth quarter of 2003, the
Company engaged Bengt Algevik to perform certain business consultancy functions
for which he received consideration, including reimbursement of travel and
other expenses, of approximately $200,000. Mr.&nbsp;Algevik completed his
assignment in May&nbsp;2004 and was appointed as a director of the Company
effective June&nbsp;16, 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, the
Company had no receivables due from Proha, which, factoring in the common stock
conversion rights of the holders of the Series&nbsp;A preferred stock (see Note
14) owns approximately 56% of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock on a
post-conversion basis.&#160; At
December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, the Company had other payables to Proha
of $0.3 million, $0.2&nbsp;million and $0.1&nbsp;million, respectively.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;1, 2004, Artemis Finland
entered into a loan agreement with a financial institution in the amount of
approximately $3.1&nbsp;million. The loan was originally due on March&nbsp;1,
2006 and accrues interest at 0.5&nbsp;percentage points above the 3-month
Euribor rate per annum, which is payable on a quarterly basis. The loan was
secured by cash collateral provided by Proha equal to the loan amount and a
security interest in substantially all of Artemis Finland&#146;s assets. Artemis and
Proha executed a letter of commitment, whereby Proha agreed to provide the
Company sufficient advance notice of its intent to demand the return of its
collateral from the financial institution.&#160;
On October&nbsp;11, 2004, the Company received a notification from Proha
declaring its intent to demand the return of its $3.1&nbsp;million collateral.
Under this notification, the Company was required to repay the loan by
January&nbsp;10, 2005. On January&nbsp;11, 2005, Artemis Finland and Proha
informed the financial institution to use the cash collateral provided by Proha
as the method by which Artemis Finland shall be deemed to have pre-paid the
loan in full. Contemporaneously, Artemis Finland entered into a Payment
Schedule Agreement (&#147;Payment Agreement&#148;) with Proha, whereby Proha effectively
replaced the financial institution as the creditor and Artemis Finland agreed
to pay Proha 2.5&nbsp;million Euros in three installments (1.25&nbsp;million
Euros by January&nbsp;17, 2005, 625,000 Euros by February&nbsp;28, 2005 and
625,000 Euros by March&nbsp;31, 2005).&#160;
The first two installments totaling approximately $2.5&nbsp;million were
paid on the due date and the Company expects to make the remaining payment
according to the Payment Agreement.&#160; The &#160;payment due on March 31, 2005 approximates
$838,000 (based on the March 15, 2005 exchange rate).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There are several related party agreements in
place between Artemis Finland and Proha or its subsidiaries and investees as
further described below:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>During
2002, Artemis Finland incurred $309,000 in fees for certain business
consulting, legal and accounting services provided by Proha.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Additionally,
Artemis Finland shares office space with Proha, for which Proha charges Artemis
Finland a share of its office-related costs (&#147;Office Allocation Charge&#148;), such
as rent, utilities, telecommunication costs, office maintenance and certain
other business costs based on headcount. The Office Allocation Charge was
$431,000, $341,000, and $290,000 for the years ended December 31, 2004, 2003
and 2002, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Accountor
Oy, a provider of accounting and payroll services, which was owned by Proha
(80.1%) and Artemis (19.9%) through November 2002 until its sale to an
unrelated party, is providing certain bookkeeping, payroll and reporting
services (&#147;Service Charge&#148;) to Artemis Finland.&#160;
The Service Charge was&#160; $0,
$80,000 and $82,000 for the years ended December 31, 2004, 2003 and 2002,
respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Intellisoft
Oy, an application service provider, which is owned by Proha (80.1%) and
Artemis (19.9%), is providing certain application hosting and other services to
Artemis Finland and its customers (&#147;ASP Services Fee&#148;). The ASP Services Fee
was&#160; $116,000, $254,000 and $354,000 for
the years ended December 31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Datamar
Oy, a subsidiary of Proha (90%), is providing certain project management and
programming services to Artemis Finland (&#147;Management Programming Fee&#148;). The
Management Programming Fee charged to Artemis Finland was $173,000, $229,000
and $340,000 for the years ended December 31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Tesnet
Group Oy (formerly Intellitest International Oy), a company partially owned by
Proha (35%), provides certain software testing services to Artemis Finland
(&#147;Testing Services&#148;).&#160; These Testing
Services were $175,000, $225,000 and $219,000 for the years ended December 31,
2004, 2003 and 2002, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Artemis
Finland is a distributor of software products provided by Safran Software
Solutions AS (&#147;Safran&#148;), a Norwegian company wholly owned by Proha. The royalty
paid by Artemis Finland to Safran was $29,000, $47,000, and $129,000 for the
years ended December 31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Artemis
Finland has provided certain software development services to ProCountor
International Oy (&#147;ProCountor&#148;), a company majority owned by Proha (63%).&#160; Artemis Finland has charged&#160; $0, $0 and $17,000 to ProCountor for such
software development services for the years ended December 31, 2004, 2003 and
2002, respectively.&#160; ProCountor has&#160; provided certain software development
services to Artemis Finland and charged a fee for use of a web-based travel and
expense claims program of $20,000, $11,000 and $0 for the years ended December
31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Artemis
Finland cooperated with Futura One Oy, a company majority owned by Proha (51%).
Artemis Finland has charged&#160; $0, $0 and
$17,000 to Futura One for software development services for the years ended
December 31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, respectively.</p>

2003 and 2002, the Company maintained the following equity holdings in joint
ventures, which are accounted for under the equity method, with the exception
of Metier Scandinavia AS (Norway) and the Metier Plancon BV, which are</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September 2000, Artemis International France Sarl
(&#147;Artemis France&#148;) entered into a joint venture agreement (the &#147;Agreement&#148;)
with the Canadian company Changepoint Corporation (&#147;Changepoint&#148;) and
established the joint venture, Changepoint France Sarl (&#147;Changepoint
France&#148;).&#160; Artemis France and Changepoint
own 40% and 60% of Changepoint France, respectively.&#160; The Agreement provides for a put and call
option for Artemis France to sell and Changepoint to purchase the 40% interest
held by Artemis France under certain conditions.&#160; </font>The Company has exercised its put
option to sell its 40% interest in Changepoint France. In May&nbsp;2004,
Compuware Corporation acquired privately held Changepoint.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company initiated arbitration proceedings
with respect to its claims and has settled this dispute subsequent to December&nbsp;31,
2004.&#160; As a result, the Company will receive
approximately $1.2 million in cash by March 31, 2005, representing the nominal
value of the shares held by Artemis France in the joint venture, shareholder
loans and other receivables owed to the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 13. Concentration of Credit
Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the years ended
December&nbsp;31, 2004, 2003 and 2002, one customer, Lockheed Martin
Corporation, accounted for approximately $3.8 million (about 7%), $5.7 million
(about 10%) and $12.3 million (about 18%), respectively, of consolidated
revenue.&nbsp; Substantially all of this revenue was generated in the Americas
segment of the Company&#146;s operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 14. Stockholders&#146; Equity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June 16, 2004 (the &#147;Closing Date&#148;), the Company
completed a private placement of $9.0 million of unregistered convertible
preferred stock (the &#147;Preferred Series A Financing&#148;).&nbsp; In connection with
this transaction, the Company issued an aggregate of 4,090,909 shares of
convertible preferred stock (the &#147;Series A Preferred Stock&#148;) to certain
accredited investors (the &#147;Series A Holders&#148;), priced at $2.20 per share, each
of which is convertible into one share of the Company&#146;s common stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, the Company issued to the Series A
Holders (i) five-year warrants to purchase an aggregate of 409,090 shares of
common stock at an exercise price of $2.64 per share (the &#147;Initial Warrants&#148;)
and (ii) 210-day warrants (the &#147;Additional Warrants&#148;) (a) that are exercisable
only in the event that the Six Month Price (as defined below) is less than
$2.20 and (b) to purchase a variable number of shares of common stock at $.01
per share based upon the Six Month Price.&nbsp; The number of issuable shares
was determined by the &#147;Six Month Price&#148; which is defined as the greater of
$1.75 or the lowest average closing price of the Company&#146;s common stock for any
15 consecutive day period during the six-month period immediately following the
Closing Date.&nbsp; The Initial Warrants vested and became fully exercisable on
the issuance date.&nbsp;As of December 15, 2004, the Six Month Price was $1.98
per share, which resulted in the issuance of 456,853 Additional Warrants to the
Series A Holders.&#160; As of December 31,
2004 certain Series A Holders exercised their Additional Warrants resulting in
the issuance of 279,188 shares of common stock.&#160;
Subsequent to year end, the remaining outstanding Additional Warrants were
exercised resulting in the issuance of 177,665 shares of common stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Proceeds from the Preferred Series A Financing
approximated $8.6 million, net of issuance costs of $0.4 million, and are being
used for (i) working capital, (ii) the repayment of debt and (iii) to
strengthen the Company&#146;s balance sheet.&nbsp; $2.2 million of the net proceeds
were transferred on behalf of Artemis directly to Laurus to pay certain
over-advances due at the Closing Date.&nbsp; (See Note 6 for more information
on the Laurus Facility).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to the Series A Preferred Stock, the
Series A Holders maintain certain powers, preferences and rights that are
senior to the holders of the Company&#146;s common stock. The Series A Holders (i)
are entitled to one vote per share on all matters upon which holders of common
stock are entitled to vote, (ii) have certain voting consents, (iii) so long as
at least twenty-five percent of Series A Preferred Stock is outstanding, have
the right to elect one member of the board of directors of the Company, and
(iv) so long as at least thirty percent of the Series A Preferred Stock is
outstanding, the Company cannot redeem or declare or pay any cash dividend or
distribution on its common stock without the prior written consent of the
holders of at least a majority of the Series A Preferred Stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The exercise prices and the number of shares
underlying the warrants are subject to anti-dilution adjustments in connection
with mergers, acquisitions, stock splits, dividends and the like.&nbsp; The
Series A Holders may pay the exercise price for the shares to be purchased upon
exercise of the warrants by paying cash equal to the number of shares to be
purchased times the appropriate exercise price per share, or, if the market
price of our common stock exceeds the exercise price to be paid per share, the
Series A Holders may, at their option, exchange the right to purchase all or
part of the maximum shares underlying the warrants for that number of shares
equal in value to the amount by which the closing price of a share of our
common stock preceding the exercise date exceeds the exercise price, multiplied
by the number of shares to be purchased at that exercise price.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company filed a registration statement on Form
S-1 with the SEC on July 19, 2004 (which was amended in August and October
2004) to register the common stock, which may be issued as described
above.&nbsp; The SEC declared such registration statement effective on October
29, 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subsequent to December 31, 2004, Laurus converted
$0.2 million of the outstanding $1.5 million Minimum Borrowing Note in exchange
for 166,700 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock (see Note 6).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2002 the Company recovered certain notes and accounts
receivable, totaling approximately $0.6 million, which had been written off
prior to the Company&#146;s reverse merger transaction in 2001.&nbsp; Since the
recovered amounts were not&#160; included in
the net assets in conjunction with the original accounting for such merger, the
recoveries were recorded as adjustments to the Company&#146;s additional paid in

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The 1998 Stock Option Plan (the &#147;1998 Plan&#148;)

As options become available due to cancellation and forfeiture, they are
added to the pool of options available for grant under the 2000 Stock Option

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;">The 2000 Stock Option Plan (the &#147;2000 Plan&#148;) provides for
the granting of incentive and non-qualified stock options to employees, board
members and advisors.&nbsp; When the 2000 Plan was adopted in March&nbsp;of
2000, it provided for the issuance of 0.3 million options.&nbsp; However, the
2000 Plan includes scheduled increases in options available for grant equal to
5% of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock to a maximum of 1.2 million
options.&nbsp; On January&nbsp;1, 2003 the 2000 Plan reached the maximum of 1.2
million options available for grant.&nbsp; In addition, 0.2 million options granted
under the 1998 Plan and subsequently cancelled are available for grant under
the 2000 Plan.&nbsp; Options granted, exercised and cancelled under the 2000
Plan are 2,206,080, 1,646 and 576,189 respectively, leaving 1,440,601 options
available under the 2000 Plan, including the cancelled 1998 Plan options, and
approximately 1,628,245 options outstanding as of December&nbsp;31, 2004.&#160; </font><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;">Effective
November 30, 2004, the 2000 Plan was amended and restated. The amended and
restated 2000 Plan provides for the issuance of 2,000,000 options, with automatic
increases (on January 1 of each year) in options available for grant equal to
5% of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock, as of the preceding December 31 up
to a maximum of 5,000,000 options.&#160;
Options granted under the 2000 Plan in 2004 include approximately
391,000 with vesting contingent upon the Company meeting certain annual
financial performance goals.</font></p>

<p style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The 2000 Non-Employee Directors&#146; Plan (the
&#147;Non-Employee Directors Plan&#148;) provides for automatic, non-discretionary grants
of up to 300,000 non-qualified stock options to non-employee board
members.&nbsp; Under the Non-Employee Directors Plan 144,900 and 41,440 options
have been granted and cancelled, respectively, and 103,460 options remain
outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2004.&#160; Effective
November&nbsp;30, 2004, the Non-Employee Directors Plan was amended and
restated. The amended and restated Non-Employee Directors Plan provides that
each Non-Employee Director who is elected or appointed to the Board after
February&nbsp;24, 2004 shall receive an initial grant of options to purchase
15,000 shares of our Common Stock. For each Non-Employee Director serving on
the Board as of February&nbsp;24, 2004, he or she received a grant of options
on February&nbsp;24, 2004 to purchase 7,500 shares of our Common Stock, unless
the Non-Employee Director was provided a special initial grant greater than
7,500 shares. Thereafter, commencing in 2005, each continuing Non-Employee
Director shall receive a grant of options on his or her Board anniversary date
to purchase up to 7,500 shares of Common Stock. With respect to directors
serving on committees, each Non-Employee Director who, on or after
February&nbsp;24, 2004, is elected or appointed as, or was already, a member of
the Audit, Compensation and/or the Nominating Committee, shall receive an
additional grant of options to purchase 3,500 shares of our Common Stock for
membership on each respective committee. Thereafter, each Non Employee Director
who continues to serve on any such committee upon his or her applicable
committee anniversary date shall be automatically granted an Option on such
anniversary date to purchase up to 3,500 shares of Common Stock.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The Company assumed non-qualified stock

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The Company also assumed non-qualified stock

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Warrants</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There were 714,096 warrants
to purchase Company common stock outstanding and exercisable at
December&nbsp;31, 2004.&#160; Other than the Additional
Warrants (see below and Note 14), the per-share exercise prices of the
remaining warrants range from $2.64 to $46.25 and they expire through 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2004, certain Series&nbsp;A Holders exercised their Additional Warrants
resulting in the issuance of 279,188 shares of common stock.&#160; Subsequent to year end the remaining
outstanding Additional Warrants were exercised, resulting in the issuance of

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is a party to a number of legal claims
arising in the ordinary course of its business.&nbsp; The Company believes the
ultimate resolution of these claims will not have a material effect on its
financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 18.&nbsp; Restructuring Costs</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In response to a decline in certain key operating
metrics such as total revenue, operating margin and revenue per employee, the
Company adopted a non-discretionary restructuring plan that resulted in a
workforce reduction and other cost reductions (collectively, the
&#147;Restructuring&#148;) intended to strengthen the Company&#146;s competitive position and
future operating performance. The Company has implemented the Restructuring
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s total charge
related to this Restructuring was approximately $2.7 million as disclosed in
the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Restructuring Charge recognized during 2004 is
comprised primarily of: (i) severance pay (including related payroll taxes) and
associated one-time employee termination costs related to the reduction of the
Company&#146;s workforce; (ii) the closure and consolidation of offices; (iii)
relocation costs resulting from organizational realignments; and (iv)
professional fees incurred to improve the competitive position of the
Company.&nbsp; The Company accounts for the costs associated with exiting an
activity, including costs associated with the reduction of the Company&#146;s
workforce, in accordance with SFAS 146.&nbsp; The following table summarizes
the Company&#146;s Restructuring-related expenses incurred during the year ended
December 31, 2004:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(A)&nbsp;Restructuring
costs for Japan/Asia have been reported in EMEA segment in Note 11 because such
costs were incurred in the United Kingdom.&#160;
The above table reflects the functional impact of the Restructuring.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This follows a similar reduction (8% of the
workforce) in the last quarter of 2003, whereby these reductions were based on
discretionary restructuring actions.&nbsp; Approximately $0.9 million of the
total restructuring charge is included in accured liabilities in the
accompanying December 31, 2004 consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GAAP prohibits the recognition of an exit-activity
liability until (a) certain criteria (which demonstrate that it is reasonably
probable that a present obligation to others has been created) are met, and (b)
the fair value of such liability can be reasonably estimated.&nbsp; The costs
associated with pre-2004 workforce reductions and related activities that did
not meet the definition of a &#147;liability&#148; (in the opinion of management) were
recorded and expensed in their natural classifications as incurred; as a
result, these expenses were not reported separately as exit-activity or
restructuring charges in the Company&#146;s consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 19.&#160;
Comprehensive Loss</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Comprehensive
loss consists of net income or loss, adjusted for other increases or decreases
affecting stockholders&#146; deficit that are excluded in the determination of net
income or loss.&#160; In July 2004, the
Company restated its comprehensive loss for the year ended December 31,
2003.&#160; The restatement was made to
correct the foreign currency translation adjustment related to the Company&#146;s
investment in Changepoint France.&#160; Such
adjustment did not affect the Company&#146;s previously reported net loss for
2003.&#160; The calculation of the restated comprehensive
loss for the year ended December 31, 2003 is as follows:</font></p>
